label: Averaging
notes: Open by naming the central tension of this appendix: a system with one slow drifting action and one fast spinning angle. The averaging method promises to ignore the wiggles and follow only the smoothed drift. Preview that the promise holds away from resonance and fails inside resonant zones, which we will make precise.

label: Fast and Slow Variables
notes: Stress the structure of the equations: the action changes at rate epsilon while the angle turns at order one. That separation of timescales is the whole hypothesis. Point out that the angle lives on a circle and the action lives in an open region, so the picture is a cylinder swept slowly sideways as the angle races around.

label: The Averaging Principle
notes: State the principle as a replacement: substitute the true right-hand side by its average over the fast angle. Emphasize that this is a recipe, not yet a theorem. The averaged system is autonomous in the action alone, vastly simpler, and our task across the next slides is to decide when its solution actually tracks the true one.

label: Phase Average
notes: Define the phase average carefully as the integral over one full turn of the angle divided by two pi. Note that it depends only on the action. Give intuition: the fast angle samples every phase nearly uniformly, so over one slow step the action feels only the mean push, and the oscillating remainder integrates away.

label: Spiral in Action Space
notes: Walk through the diagram. The true trajectory spirals because the fast angle keeps winding while the action creeps outward. The averaged guiding path is the smooth radial drift through the center of the coils. Make the learner see that averaging is literally collapsing the spiral onto its slowly moving guiding curve.

label: Error Estimate
notes: Give the headline estimate: the gap between true and averaged actions stays of order epsilon over a time of order one over epsilon. So on the natural slow timescale the approximation is uniformly good. Underline that the time interval grows as epsilon shrinks, which is exactly the regime where the slow drift becomes visible.

label: Justification Sketch
notes: Sketch the change of variables that removes the oscillating part. We add a small periodic correction of order epsilon to the action, chosen so its derivative cancels the fluctuating remainder. What survives is the averaged drift plus terms of order epsilon squared, and integrating those over the long time gives the order epsilon bound.

label: Resonance Breaks Averaging
notes: Now the warning. The correction term divides by the frequency, so when the frequency passes through zero or a rational combination vanishes, the small denominator explodes. Inside such resonant zones the oscillation no longer averages out, the trajectory can be captured or kicked, and the simple averaged drift loses its predictive power.

label: Many Frequencies
notes: Generalize to several fast angles. Now resonances form a dense web of planes in frequency space where integer combinations vanish. Averaging is trustworthy on the complement of a thin neighborhood of that web. Mention that controlling the measure of the resonant set is the heart of the deeper Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser and Nekhoroshev theory.

label: Adiabatic Invariants
notes: Connect to adiabatic theory. When the system has an action-angle structure and a slowly varying parameter, the action is approximately conserved precisely because the averaged drift of the action vanishes. The pendulum with slowly shortening string is the classic example: energy over frequency stays nearly constant through the slow change.

label: Celestial Mechanics
notes: Bring in the historical engine. Planetary orbits have fast orbital angles and slowly drifting orbital elements like eccentricity and perihelion. Averaging over the fast orbital motion yields the secular equations that predict long-term precession. Resonances between orbital periods are exactly where this averaging program runs into its famous small-divisor trouble.

label: Summary
notes: Recap the arc: separate fast and slow, average the slow drift over the angle, and trust the result for times of order one over epsilon away from resonance. Leave the learner with the two-sided lesson: averaging is a powerful simplification and a precise warning sign wherever frequencies lock together.
